captions.text: All right. We are set — your shared screen is up on the projectile motion notes, part two. It shows the three results we're about to talk through.
What does the range formula give if I put in a hundred and twenty degrees?
I'll check that quickly.
For a hundred twenty degrees, the formula gives a negative range, meaning it goes to the left. The magnitude is root three over two times v zero squared over g.
Do the units of the range formula actually work out?
Do the units of the range formula actually work out?
Mm-hmm.
Let me just check that. Yes. V zero squared over g has units
of meters, and sine of two theta has no units, so the range comes out in meters, which is what we want.
They do. V zero squared over g gives meters, and the sine factor is dimensionless, so the range ends up in meters.
We're back on setup. On your shared screen now: projectile motion, the setup and initial conditions.

I'll take a look.
